items.title: Lymph node contraction links sex-biased naive CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell decline to compromised antigen recognition during middle age
items.author: Timothy P. Padera
items.content: Menzel and colleagues report that male mice and humans undergo accelerated immune aging, characterized by naive CD8+ T cell decline and early thymic involution, which impairs cancer antigen recognition and response to immunotherapy.

items.title: Naive T cell decline limits cancer immunity in middle-aged male mice
items.content: Using mice and supporting human data, we show that accelerated loss of naive CD8+ T cells in male mice leads to lymph node contraction and limited cancer antigen recognition. Restoring thymic output replenished naive CD8+ T cells and improved responses to immunotherapy in middle-aged male mice.

items.title: Which is better: Buying or renting a home? - Ella Feldman
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into the dilemma of whether it's financially better to rent or buy a home, and explore the pros and cons of each choice.

--

Nobody was surprised when Morgan and her twin sister Lisa moved into identical houses right next to each other. The only difference? Morgan bought her house, while Lisa is renting hers. For generations, conventional wisdom has been that homeownership is financially better than renting. But is this actually true? Ella Feldman follows the twins in their housing journey to see who comes out on top.

Lesson by Ella Feldman, directed by Josh Pilch, Augenblick Studios.

items.title: Heterogeneity in secondary follicle development buffers the lifespan of activated oocytes to optimize female fertility in mice
items.author: Hua Zhang
items.content: Liang, Yang and colleagues map the developmental dynamics of activated oocytes and folliculogenesis across the reproductive lifespan using lineage tracing in mice. Their work reveals marked heterogeneity in the lifespan of activated oocytes in growing follicles, which form a secondary ovarian reserve that buffers oocyte utilization and sustains fertility.

items.title: Why is Queen Victoria so controversial? - Carolyn Harris
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Queen Victoria presided over a golden age of the British Empire — but was she its moral compass or obsessed with her reputation?

--

During her 63-year reign, Queen Victoria was a model of morality and restraint. So much so that the 19th century is called the “Victorian Age” and is still associated with these qualities. But was she the empire’s moral compass during a time of dizzying change, or an imperialist monarch who cared more about her reputation than her subjects? Carolyn Harris puts this controversial figure on trial.

Lesson by Carolyn Harris, directed by Igor Ćorić, Artrake Studio.

items.title: Это ДОКАЗЫВАЕТ симуляцию! 5 признаков — Профессор Хоффман
items.content:
В новом выпуске — разговор с Дональдом Хоффманом, когнитивным психологом, профессором-эмеритом Калифорнийского университета в Ирвайне и исследователем сознания и зрительного восприятия. Поговорили о его главной идее: эволюция могла сформировать наше восприятие не для того, чтобы показывать реальность такой, какая она есть, а для того, чтобы помогать нам выживать.

Обсудили, почему окружающий мир можно сравнить с интерфейсом или VR-гарнитурой, действительно ли пространство и время фундаментальны и может ли сознание существовать независимо от привычной нам физической реальности. Дональд объяснил, почему два человека могут совершенно по-разному воспринимать один и тот же цвет, хотя называют его одинаково, и почему мы никогда не можем точно знать, каким мир видит другой человек.

Также поговорили о сознании животных, искусственном интеллекте, гипотезе симуляции, смерти и о том, почему современная наука до сих пор не может объяснить происхождение субъективного опыта. Разобрались, насколько сильно наше восприятие упрощает окружающий мир и может ли реальность за пределами привычных пространства и времени оказаться принципиально сложнее всего, что мы способны увидеть.

items.title: Why are AI data centers using so much electricity? - Sajan Saini
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore the challenges and possibilities of AI data centers, and how these rapidly expanding complexes use energy and resources.

--

Since 2019, over a thousand warehouse campuses have popped up around the world. Each complex covers nearly 100,000 square meters, uses as much water as a small town, and as much electricity as a small city. These are AI data centers — facilities for running and training Large Language Models like ChatGPT. Sajan Saini explores the challenges and possibilities of these rapidly expanding complexes.

items.title: Why magnets stumped scientists for so long - Rachel Yang
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore the physics of magnetism, and how its properties are used in modern technologies like MRI machines, hard drives, and more.

--

In the 1920s, physicists still had many unanswered questions about magnetism. While they knew that every electron and proton have invisible, magnetic fields that radiate out in closed loops from one end to the other, they wondered: what determines the direction of these magnetic fields? And if every atom is composed of these tiny magnets, why isn’t everything magnetic? Rachel Yang investigates.

items.title: Everything you need to know about bird flu - Benjamin Anderson
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into the science of avian influenza to find out what makes the H5N1 virus so dangerous, and its potential to jump to humans.

--

While avian influenza used to infect mostly birds, in the past few years, it’s been found in over 70 mammal species, including cats, dairy cows, foxes, seals, and bears. Each new mammalian infection gives the virus more chances to drift or shift, spill over into humans, and ignite a pandemic. So, what is it about H5N1 that makes it so frighteningly flexible? Benjamin Anderson investigates.

Lesson by Benjamin Anderson, directed by Anton Bogaty.

В этом выпуске я поделюсь личным опытом диагностики аутоиммунного заболевания кишечника и разберу недавний диагноз известного биохакера Брайана Джонсона — аутоиммунный гастрит.  

Почему иммунная система начинает атаковать собственный организм? Какую роль в этом играют гены, половые гормоны и перенесённые инфекции? В видео мы детально разоблачим 10 популярных мифов об аутоиммунных болезнях и разберём как существующие методы лечения, так и экспериментальные технологии будущего — CAR-T-терапию и трансплантацию стволовых клеток.

items.title: Why do some people have a better sense of direction than others? - Oliver Baumann
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into the neuroscience behind our sense of direction and find out why some people are better at navigating than others.

--

Whether you identify as a wayfinding whiz or get lost returning from the grocery store, your brain has a built-in navigation system that facilitates spatial skills, from sensing which direction is north to map-reading and route-learning. So, why do we still struggle to find our way? And why do some of us find ourselves lost more often than others? Oliver Baumann digs into our sense of direction.

Lesson by Oliver Baumann, directed by Anton Bogaty.
